classes.core: Removing it breaks the Tower contract. It is never a switch.
classes.optional-component: A capability whose off state leaves the rest of Tower intact. It must be a user-visible switch with a documented fallback.
classes.optional-config: A tuning knob, not a capability. It stays in the config form and never hides a component.
classes.forbidden-to-disable: The host, the health contract, the recovery escape and the merge gates. No group, row or boolean key may turn it off.

components.fallback: Off equals uninstalling Tower: no tools, presets or skills remain. That is the accepted all-off boundary of the mandatory host anchor, not an optional capability.
The Host plugin itself, nested under the mandatory tower anchor. A mandatory dependency, never its own switch.
The 3 skills leave the catalog; the worker/reviewer PROTOCOL sections still ship through systemPrompt.section, so only the tower-recovery guidance is lost.
tower_batch is not registered; missions, gates and merges are unaffected because no state depends on a batch.
tower_import_legacy and tower_legacy_map are not registered; new repository state is unaffected.

tower_resource is not registered; advisory leases are coordination only, but spawn.requireLease still needs the tool to acquire one, so a config that sets spawn.requireLease is rejected at runtime preconditions instead of failing every spawn at lease-busy.
tower_test is not registered and no test receipt can be recorded. With gates.requireTests:true planning/mode entry is rejected with an explanation, and the merge gate still reports tests-missing.

MISSIONS.md is not written or refreshed, so an existing board goes stale. Mission state tools, gates and every other capability keep working; docs.boardLocation still chooses where a board would be written.

Terminal missions are not moved out of state.json, so the hot state keeps growing and status/doctor keep loading their full history. Merges, gates and every other capability keep working; nothing is deleted. afterDays/maxMissions keep their tuning meaning.

Development-only tooling: tower_reload and /tower reload are unavailable, so a linked-profile reload has to be triggered outside Tower. A normal profile behaves exactly as before; the row ships disabled on purpose.
Declared by dsh-tower/preset-worker: tower_spawn fails without the worker preset. A mandatory dependency, never a switch.

Declared by dsh-tower/preset-reviewer: the reviewer cannot be dispatched. Supported while review.mode is off or optional (merge is unaffected; off does not use the preset at all); with review.mode required, planning/mode entry is locked with an explanatory error.
The Tower web UI plugin does not load in this profile: no Tower tool cards, composer-dock summary or status strip. Host tools, missions, state and the MISSIONS.md board are unaffected.

keys.name: section
keys.note: Legacy alias for mode.promptSection: the Tower-mode prompt contract, not a capability.

keys.name: allowAgentControl
keys.note: Legacy alias for mode.allowAgentControl: the human-owned mode rule (ADR 0003), not a component.

keys.name: init.autoGitInit
keys.note: Bootstrap convenience; off only means tower_init will not run git init.

exemption.reason: Tuning, not capability: tower_init stays the component and the switch only decides whether it runs git init.

keys.name: init.snapshotDirty
keys.note: Dirty-work baseline convenience; no capability is removed.

exemption.reason: Tuning, not capability: the init component remains available with or without a dirty-work snapshot baseline.

keys.name: init.autoExclude
keys.note: Keeps Tower artifacts out of .git/info/exclude; safe either way.

exemption.reason: Tuning, not capability: both values keep the init component and only change which artifacts the exclude file names.

keys.name: mode.promptSection
keys.note: Replaces the whole Tower-mode prompt text; contract text, not a capability.

keys.name: mode.sectionAppend
keys.note: Appends team conventions to the prompt.

keys.name: mode.allowAgentControl
keys.note: Decides whether the model may toggle the mode (ADR 0003). A governance rule, never a component.

keys.name: mode.autoPauseGoal
keys.note: Entering the mode pauses an active goal; exit never resumes it.

keys.name: mode.requireResumeAuthorization
keys.note: Guards resuming a user-paused mission.

keys.name: mode.requireHumanAckOnFirstEntry
keys.note: First entry can require an explicit human ack.

keys.name: mode.workspaceLock
keys.note: One Tower session per repository is a safety contract; a row may not turn it off.

keys.name: mode.workspaceLockScope
keys.note: Chooses whether read-only tools take the workspace lock.

keys.name: mode.planModePolicy
keys.note: Plan mode and Tower mode stay mutually exclusive.

keys.name: mode.workspaceStaleMs
keys.note: Stale window for the advisory workspace lock.

keys.name: mode.heartbeatMs
keys.note: Heartbeat interval while the mode is on.

keys.name: mode.denyTools
keys.note: The denied-tool list is part of the mode guard.

keys.name: mode.storePath
keys.note: Custom mode-store location; no capability is removed.

keys.name: mode.maxEntries
keys.note: Bounds the persisted mode store.

keys.name: mode.lockTimeoutMs
keys.note: Bounded wait for the cross-process mode lock.

keys.name: review.mode
keys.note: The review policy: off, optional (default) or required, selected by one tri-state control on the plugin-page configuration form. It is configuration, not a component row and not three mutually exclusive rows. off intentionally removes tower_review, refuses reviewer spawn and makes the merge gate ignore review; optional never blocks a merge; required makes a clean tip-bound review a merge blocker. The reviewer preset row stays a capability the mode may leave unused.

keys.name: review.requireReview
keys.note: Deprecated one-release boolean alias for review.mode (true -> required, false -> optional; default optional). It is policy configuration and a deprecated alias, not a switch a row may own; false never overrides an explicit mode. Kept so 2.5 configurations keep working; remove after the 2.6 alias window.

keys.name: review.maxRoundsPerReviewer
keys.note: Caps review rounds; part of the review contract.

keys.name: merge.timeoutMs
keys.note: Default merge timeout; a per-call value wins.

keys.name: merge.maxBufferBytes
keys.note: Captured merge output buffer.

keys.name: git.timeoutMs
keys.note: Default Git command timeout outside merge.

keys.name: worktrees.root
keys.note: Default worktree placement.

keys.name: spawn.workerPreset
keys.note: Chooses the worker tool surface; a dependency, never a switch.

keys.name: spawn.reviewerPreset
keys.note: Chooses the read-only reviewer surface; a dependency, never a switch.

keys.name: spawn.maxDepth
keys.note: Subagent depth requested at spawn.

keys.name: spawn.provider
keys.note: Provider route for spawned agents.

keys.name: spawn.workerModel
keys.note: Optional model route for workers.

keys.name: spawn.reviewerModel
keys.note: Optional independent model route for reviewers.

keys.name: spawn.maxLiveWorkers
keys.note: Resource-safety cap on live workers.

keys.name: spawn.staleMs
keys.note: Roster staleness window before merge is blocked.

keys.name: spawn.maxWaitMs
keys.note: Upper bound for a blocking spawn wait.

keys.name: spawn.requireLease
keys.note: Advisory-lease gate before a worker starts.

exemption.reason: Tuning the safety level inside the optional tower-leases row; with leases off the Host refuses requireLease instead of removing the spawn capability.

keys.name: send.maxPerMinute
keys.note: Message rate limit; zero disables it.

keys.name: send.interruptDefault
keys.note: Default for the interrupt-before-deliver flag.

exemption.reason: Tuning, not capability: the send component always exists and the switch only picks a delivery default.

keys.name: tests.admission
keys.note: Chooses when discovery runs inside the optional tests capability.

exemption.reason: Tuning when the admission check runs inside the optional tower-tests row, which still owns whether test tooling exists.

keys.name: tests.timeoutMs
keys.note: Per-command discovery timeout.

keys.name: tests.maxBytes
keys.note: Captured discovery output cap.

keys.name: tests.autoChecks
keys.note: Attaches a tests check to completion when discovery runs.

exemption.reason: Tuning the default receipt policy inside the optional tower-tests row, which still owns whether any test tooling exists.

keys.name: tests.allowPackageDiscovery
keys.note: Allows repository code to execute; a security contract, not a component.

keys.name: gates.requireChecks
keys.note: Requires completion evidence before merge; a merge gate.

keys.name: gates.requireTests
keys.note: Requires a test receipt before merge; a merge gate. With the tower-tests row off, planning/mode entry refuse the combination.

keys.name: gates.allowReviewExemption
keys.note: The review-exemption path is part of the review and merge contract.

keys.name: gates.maxReportBytes
keys.note: The report cap is part of the completion contract; the refusal itself is never configurable away.

keys.name: docs.boardLocation
keys.note: Chooses where the board is written; whether it is written is the tower-board component row (#133).

keys.name: archive.afterDays
keys.note: Archive age threshold inside the optional tower-archive component (#135).

keys.name: archive.maxMissions
keys.note: Hot terminal-mission cap.

keys.name: leases.ttlMs
keys.note: Tuning inside the optional tower-leases component.

keys.name: dev.reloadDelayMs
keys.note: Delay so a tool result is delivered before a scheduled reload inside the optional tower-hmr component.

keys.name: dev.reloadRequiredIds
keys.note: Loader ids passed to reconcileProfile as required by the tower-hmr component.

forbidden.reason: Without the host the plugin registers nothing; there is no off state that leaves the rest working, and no config boolean may remove it. The visible `tower` anchor is the all-off boundary, and the host section nested under it may never become its own switch.
Diagnosis must always exist so a failure message can point at it. #122 removed exposeDoctor and the exposeOperational master switch; the tool is registered for every configuration.
The escape hatch must exist whenever the lock it repairs can be left behind. #122 removed exposeRecovery and the exposeOperational master switch; the tool is registered for every configuration.

forbidden.capability: the review gate in required mode
forbidden.reason: The policy is one tri-state configuration control on the plugin-page form, not a component row: review.mode is off, optional (default) or required, and off is a documented mode that removes tower_review and makes the merge gate ignore review. What no group, row or boolean key may switch off is the gate once the mode is required: a completed mission still needs a clean review bound to the branch tip, and the exemption path stays explicit. review.requireReview is a deprecated one-release alias, not a switch. The reviewer preset row remains a capability the policy may leave unused, never a way to weaken required mode.
gates.* decides delivery; a component may not bypass it.
